# Safety Controls & Devices Limited
## 1. Executive Verdict

**Hold — unresolved. Not rank-eligible; no current buy recommendation.** Safety Controls & Devices Limited is an electrical-infrastructure EPC contractor, not a safety-equipment manufacturer with a demonstrated recurring product franchise. Its apparent low earnings multiple is not sufficient compensation evidence when cash conversion, historical accounting and current funding cannot be reconciled reliably.

FY26 revenue increased to ₹117.01 crore and PAT to ₹14.42 crore. Yet CFO was **negative ₹11.22 crore**, trade receivables plus retention reached **₹158.71 crore**, and unrestricted cash was only **₹0.22 crore** at 31 March 2026. A ₹48 crore fresh IPO followed in April. This changes the funding picture materially, but audited March cash cannot be added to gross IPO money and called October unrestricted cash. Fees, restricted objects, debt repayment and subsequent working-capital use matter.

The strongest adverse evidence is the original FY25 ₹16.56 crore vendor-loss charge to reserves, subsequent restatement differences, a genuine February 2026 bank-guarantee/overutilisation default, and weak cash conversion. The strongest counterevidence is equally important: the lender confirmed regularisation on 13 April, Acuité upgraded to BB+/Stable/A4+ on 31 August after the curing period, and FY26 carries an unmodified audit opinion and satisfactory IFC opinion. **Historical default is not a claim of current default; accounting contradictions are not proof of fraud.** [E01–E10]

The common-entry monthly model gives no ordinary shareholder return for the base case because terminal debt retirement and operating reserves are not cash-funded. The bull case survives and produces a conditional ₹213.72 exit price and 21.03% net annual return, but requires better collections and margins than a conservative underwriting case. It is a hypothesis to falsify, not a price target.

## 4. Business Overview

Safety designs, procures, installs, tests and commissions electrical substations and allied works. Its disclosed technical envelope includes AIS substations up to 400 kV and GIS up to 220 kV, with solar, fire-fighting and hospital/infrastructure work. These are principally project businesses: qualification and award lead to equipment procurement, construction, certification, milestone billing and collection. They are not subscription revenues. Management reports 19 commissioned substations and 60 employees; outsourced suppliers and project execution resources are therefore important. [RHP pp 136–156; E11]

A sale is not cash. Percentage-of-completion/certification, customer advances, vendor advances and 15–30% retention terms produce long financing cycles. Materials consumed were ₹81.25 crore against FY26 revenue ₹117.01 crore. Procurement pass-through and changing contract mix can move sales and margins without equivalent proprietary value added. Public-sector/utility customers can lower ultimate counterparty-loss risk while increasing certification and payment timing risk. Principal disclosed geography is Uttar Pradesh and Bihar; government tender demand does not guarantee company-level order access or settlement.

No material acquisition, amalgamation, divestment or revaluation is identified over the disclosed ten-year lookback. The RHP says there are no subsidiaries/associates and at one point no joint venture, but separately describes a 19 January 2024 joint-bid deed with K. Ramachandra Rao Transmission & Projects Private Limited for BSPTCL NIT 38/PR/2023 with joint/several responsibilities. This could be a contractual consortium rather than an equity JV. We do not invent an acquired subsidiary or conclude the obligations are zero. Obtain the deed, work-share and guarantee schedule before closing scope risk. [RHP pp 174–175; E12]

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

Tender credentials, technical capability, bank-guarantee access and completion history create real entry friction. They do not establish switching costs, pricing power, brand dominance or recurring service economics. In FY25 the largest customer represented 65.07% of revenue, the largest three 94.10%, and top five 97.80%; the largest supplier represented 56.64% of purchase/direct-expense concentration and top three 66.61%. The supplier table's misleading column label is not treated as a revenue ratio. Ten months to January 2026 top customer concentration eased to 41.55%, but top three remained 90.91%. [RHP; E11]

There is no verified market-share numerator/denominator, proprietary-IP economic record or price-volume realization bridge. MOAT 4 reflects a capable small contractor with qualifications, not a demonstrated protected franchise. Further growth may require both more procurement credit and more BG collateral, limiting the apparent asset-light advantage.

## 6. Revenue Growth & Scale

Reported net-GST revenue grew from ₹47.88 crore FY23 to ₹44.71 crore FY24, ₹102.56 crore FY25 and ₹117.01 crore FY26. The three-year CAGR is **34.70%**, using exactly three annual intervals. Annual additions are −₹3.16 crore, +₹57.85 crore and +₹14.45 crore. FY24 contracted 6.61%, FY25 increased 129.38%, and FY26 increased 14.09%. This is uneven project scaling, not a stable 35% annual engine. [E02,E21]

The revenue endpoints are same-entity and net-GST, and FY25 revenue reconciles between original and restated records. No acquired revenue is identified, making organic-like entity growth the defensible basis, with Medium confidence. An exact organic volume/real-price split is **not** available: equipment prices, pass-through procurement, contract mix and POC recognition could contribute. Thus the report does not call 34.70% underlying physical-volume growth.

Original FY21 sales were ₹32.25314 crore, not the rounded ₹27 crore sometimes displayed by aggregators, but the GST/presentation basis cannot be reconciled sufficiently to FY26. Five-year CAGR is NS rather than a selectively convenient number. Ten-year CAGR is also NS. FY23 original, later-comparative and prospectus profits/cash differ; these cannot be used interchangeably to claim a decade of quality growth. The listed history since April 2026 is too short to infer stable trading or minority-shareholder outcomes.

RHP current orders included TUSCO ₹83.53 crore dated 19 August 2025 and RVNL ₹55.65 crore dated 19 December 2025. The later Acuité aggregate unexecuted order book was ₹327.62 crore at 31 July 2026 versus ₹314.81 crore a year earlier. These dates/scopes differ, so the two orders are not added to the total and the old single-order DRHP table is not called current backlog. A complete opening backlog + intake − execution − cancellation bridge and project-level margin/collection schedule remain ND. [E13]

## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

The growth opportunity is real: transmission/substation additions and renewable grid integration require EPC capacity. But company-level reinvestment is dominated by working capital and collateral, not just PPE. FY26 cash capex was only ₹0.0351 crore; this does not explain negative CFO, nor establish that growth needs no capital. FY26 IC grew ₹36.42 crore, driven by ₹37.33 crore additional operating working capital while restricted-BG deposits released ₹0.56 crore. [financial_inputs.json reinvestment_bridges]

IC is reconciled from both sides with component-level records. Financing IC = equity + gross debt + net DTL + income-tax provision − unrestricted cash; required restricted BG collateral remains invested capital. Asset-side IC includes PPE, collateral, receivables, retention, inventory, vendor/government/security advances and prepaids, less non-interest operating liabilities. FY26 financing IC is ₹113.8132 crore versus asset-side ₹113.8133 crore, a ₹0.0001 crore rounding difference. FY25 original opening IC ₹77.3974 crore yields average IC ₹95.6053 crore. At an explicit 25.17% normalized tax assumption, FY26 EBIT ₹26.0469 crore gives NOPAT ₹19.4909 crore and indicative ROIC **20.39%**. This is not an audited project IRR. [E01,E03,E24]

Reinvestment bridges, in ₹ lakh: FY24 restated ΔIC 1565.57 = .53 capex −14.96 DA +1689.68 ΔONWC −106.09 BG −3.61 security +.02 rounding. FY25 restated ΔIC 2956.07 = 472.03 −31.60 +2256.03 +264.02 −4.40 −.01. FY26 original ΔIC 3641.61 = 3.51 −37.18 +3732.67 −56.17 −1.22. Financing and asset components are retained for every observation, not reconstructed from revenue multiples.

The one-year incremental proxy is ΔNOPAT/ΔIC using original FY25–26; it is diagnostic only because margin improvement, old-contract recognition and reserve losses distort causation. A valid three/five-year incremental-return numerator and denominator cannot be isolated across the accounting discontinuities. CAP remains NS. No high ROIC is used to give a second boost to REV or a compounder designation.

The forecast requires incremental fixed capital above an explicitly hypothetical ₹150 crore sales envelope, maintenance capex and full target operating working capital; added capacity faces a three-month qualification lag. These are A, not management disclosed capacity plans. Growth earns value only if incremental cash returns exceed the 16–22% model discount rate; faster sales financed by mounting receivables can destroy rather than create value.

## 8. Management, Governance & Execution

Promoters held 9,199,305 shares or 46.40% in the issuer's 10 April 2026 pattern. The official October capital master reconciles total issued shares, but the April 15,410,999 locked shares are not treated as October free float. No unverified pledge-free/current-beneficial-holding assertion is made. [E15,E16]

The major stewardship question is the FY25 ₹16.5565 crore vendor-advance loss charged directly to reserves. On the original FY25 result, charging that loss through profit would turn ₹7.6441 crore PAT into an approximately ₹8.9124 crore loss. The prospectus restatement instead assigns ₹2.2335 crore loss to FY23 and ₹2.8863 crore to FY24, with earlier losses in opening reserves. Those losses are not charged again to FY25 in this analysis. Counterparty identity, relatedness, board approval, recoverability attempts and allocation rationale require primary records. This is a documented treatment issue, not a finding of diversion or fraud. [E03]

FY26 MD remuneration was ₹34 lakh, Abhishek remuneration ₹16.2 lakh, and sitting fees ₹10.2 lakh. The MD loan bridge broadly reconciles: opening 69.81 + received 296.56 − repaid 100.69 = 265.68 lakh, close to note 6/board 265.67 but not note 27's 262.19. Note 6 classifies short-term, whereas the board narrative says non-current. Anjali remuneration 3.25 lakh in the board table versus nil in note 27 also needs reconciliation. These are specific small inconsistencies, not an invented large RPT siphoning. Proposed MD compensation from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2029 was fixed ₹80 lakh plus 2% of Section 198 profit and business reimbursements; AGM approval outcome is unverified, so proposed terms are not called approved. [E06]

Earlier RPT history is also qualified: the FY24 original note28 shows Rajnish remuneration ₹60 lakh, Anjali ₹1.2 lakh and Abhishek ₹16.2 lakh in each of FY23 and FY24. FY24 Rajnish loans taken ₹147.05 lakh and repaid ₹96.40 lakh suggest a ₹50.65 lakh movement, but the printed table places ₹50.65 lakh under FY23 receivable, with no FY24 closing payable. That anomalous layout is preserved, not silently repaired into a promoter-loan roll-forward. FY22 note25 RPT tables are effectively blank, which is not evidence that no transactions occurred. Full five-year RPT completeness is therefore not established. [O22 note25; O24 note28]

Audit trail by year: FY21 unmodified with COVID emphasis; CARO referenced but missing from the accessible original, IFC clean. FY22 unmodified/CARO read; referenced IFC and own cash-flow page missing. FY23 unmodified/CARO/IFC; edit-log rule not yet applicable until April 2023. FY24 qualified for GST-inclusive grossing, IFC described as inapplicable, edit-log wording only confirms a feature. The issuer FY25 file does not include the full original opinion/CARO/IFC; RHP disclosure and the original reserve note are not substitutes for claiming the missing original opinion was read. FY26 unmodified opinion and satisfactory IFC, but CARO records Canara payment delays ₹290,840 for 56 days and ₹286,359 for 28 days, no internal-audit system, and audit-trail feature existence rather than complete operation/tamper/preservation assurance. [E04,E05; original_audit_extract.json]

RHP discloses Doshi resignation 11 August 2025 and Panchal appointment 12 August; FY26 CARO says no auditor resignation. The resolution could concern scope/timing/interpretation, but no reconciliation is supplied. RHP and final prospectus no-default assertions conflict with the subsequently established February bank event. Note 32's ₹200 lakh FY25 Section 42 penalty becomes nil FY26, while RHP describes cheque, tax and ROC matters. Nil closing accounting balance or audit wording is not a settlement order. Obtain orders and current case status before claiming clearance. [E05–E10]

Execution is measured by collection as well as awards. The prospectus FY26 receivable projection ₹96.52 crore was below actual ₹121.60 crore excluding retention, a ₹25.08 crore miss. Forecast 240 days and agency 379 days use potentially different denominators; they are not subtracted as if identical. Low material cost helped FY26 margin expansion; sustained project economics, rather than a procurement-price benefit alone, must be demonstrated.

It comprises ₹17 crore funded limits and ₹83 crore nonfunded limits, not ₹100 crore free cash. Bank utilisation 87.98% funded/77.09% nonfunded is 9-month average through July, not committed available October headroom. [E07–E10]

## 10. Valuation & Market Expectations

At conditional ₹79.06 and 19,826,999 shares, market capitalisation is ₹156.75 crore. Current-share FY26 P/E is 10.87× and ex-prior-tax-credit 11.69×. The common shortcut 79.06/10.60 materially understates P/E after IPO dilution. March debt/cash plus October post IPO market cap produces only a stale-date EV bridge, not current EV. Neither EPS normalisation nor a low multiple resolves negative cash conversion or source discrepancies. R and P remain NS.

### Funding and timing model

All scenarios start with 31 March 2026 observed balances and the same seven-period analytical bridge to 19 October 2026. No H1FY27 cash flow was available within cutoff. April 1–12 daily cash movements are unobserved; IPO availability on 13 April is assumed from listing/cure chronology, not bank statement. Ordinary April flows settle on 30 April. This explicit gap means the model is not a verified historical survival reconstruction. Post entry bear/base/bull divergence begins 20 October and first modeled payment 19 November 2026.

Opening available cash ₹.2209 crore is separate from ₹14.4084 crore pledged FD and ₹.3481 crore government advance, neither spent. IPO gross ₹48 crore less detailed fees ₹5.76 crore yields ₹42.24 crore earmarked: ₹6 crore debt repayment, ₹31.5 crore eligible WC and ₹4.74 crore GCP. Actual gross issuance is not issued twice in shares. WC proceeds release only against supplier/operating cash payments, not again as a reduction of ΔWC. Unspent pools are excluded from terminal cash. The competing ₹43.14 crore net-proceeds summary is tested as ₹.90 crore fee relief, not silently used. Fees ex/inclusive GST wording is ambiguous; an additional ₹1.0368 crore 18%-of-detailed-fee sensitivity is also retained. Already incurred ₹.207 crore IPO expenses are within the fee budget, not added again. [E14]

Opening statutory dues ₹4.0466 crore settle 30 April A; income tax ₹6.087 crore in four ₹1.52175 crore installments June/September/December/March A; current gratuity ₹.10 crore September A. Prepayment fee ₹.24 crore is 4% of ₹6 crore A, separate from principal and IPO fees. Long gratuity ₹.2322 crore is retained terminal claim. Payroll/expense/customer-advance liabilities remain in ONWC and are not paid a second time. First year current maturities ₹5.0161 crore are modeled monthly in addition to IPO ₹6 crore repayment, with 0/50/100% overlap sensitivities because exact facility allocation is unverified. Full overlap preserves more terminal debt, not free cash. Remaining opening debt incurs 20% annual interest A, sensitised 16–24%, and is cash-retired once at terminal. April charges the full opening debt for 12 days before the assumed 13 April repayment and the post-repayment balance for 18 days; this adds ₹0.03945 crore versus incorrectly applying the lower debt throughout April. Actual penal interest and bank debit dates remain unverified.

Each month has two supplier front/collection cycles; 60% of cost is paid before each collection. Every event checks ₹.10 crore minimum cash, not just year-end. Receivables, inventory, retention/vendor assets, payables and accruals are explicit stock rollforwards. Growth fixed capex pays upfront above the ₹150 crore inflation-adjusted envelope at ₹.06 per incremental revenue ₹1; qualification lag 3 months. Maintenance is max(.5% sales, 5% opening PPE); depreciation 8% PPE; tax 25.17% on positive profit, with no invented tax-loss refund. These are assumptions, not audited contractual terms.

Existing ₹14.4084 crore BG collateral remains blocked. Additional cash-funded collateral rises with peak annual revenue above the audited ₹117.0147 crore base, at 15% / 10% / 8% in bear / base / bull. No release is assumed. It is a separate intraperiod payment, does not qualify for IPO working-capital releases in this model, enters operating capital, and is reinvested at terminal growth. Ratios 0% / 5% / 15% / 20% are separately tested. At terminal, additional collateral reinvestment equals growth × collateral ratio × the greater of final-year realised revenue and ending annual sales run-rate. This retains the full marginal requirement, rather than growing only collateral above the historical revenue offset. It replaces, rather than adds to, g × existing additional collateral within terminal ONWC growth. Actual bank collateral terms are ND; assuming no additional collateral silently would overstate growth affordability.

## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The strongest bear case is that apparently profitable EPC growth keeps consuming cash through uncertified receivables, retention and vendor advances; a supplier or BG event then forces repayment while tender customers delay cash. Historical vendor loss and February BG invocation show this mechanism is not purely abstract. A 35% revenue fall is below the FY25 largest customer 65.07% exposure, but is still an analyst stress, not a forecast customer loss. Receivable 10%/inventory 10% haircuts and ₹5 crore BG call are assumptions, not discovered impairments.

The no-finance stress breaches a supplier front payment; bounded bank/equity only delays breach. Capital can then be impaired through forced asset collection discounts, lien priority, project termination penalties, dilutive capital or insolvency costs. We do not report a normal IRR after such breach. The balance-sheet book equity is not a liquidation floor: BG FD is encumbered, receivables require certification, current liabilities and statutory claims have priority, and missing claim details prevent a robust net recoverable value. Downside can be severe, including complete equity loss; no fabricated probability is assigned.

The decisive thesis-break variable is **cash collection net of new working-capital commitments**, not revenue or announced orders. Countercase: public clients eventually settle, IPO working capital restores execution and Acuite upgrade persists. Evidence needed to choose between these cases is post-cutoff monitoring, not optimistic multiple expansion at the cutoff.

## 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility

Required gross price CAGRs are 37.97% for 5× in 5 years, 58.49% for 10× in 5 years, 17.46% for 5× in 10 years and 25.89% for 10× in 10 years. Net return after costs is lower; dilution means enterprise growth must outpace per share growth. Tests use both base and bull cash economics, 10/20/30/40/50/60% sales growth, both horizons and both targets. They retain every trial's revenue, new operating capital, finance debt/equity/fees, shares, survival and 8× EBIT lower-multiple crosscheck.

Very high growth requires additional qualified projects, BG access, procurement credit, staffing and collection capacity; a ₹327.62 crore July backlog does not establish decade-long replenishment. Any mathematically successful bull trial is classified **Speculative / unsupported**, not a multibagger candidate, until comparable accounts, sustainable incremental returns and funded order access are demonstrated. ## 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action

**Hold — unresolved; not a compounder; not an investable or multibagger ranking entry.** BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS with explicit coverage and bounds. A governance Avoid label would require stronger substantiated adverse evidence, while a clean low P/E buy would require much better reliability, cash and execution evidence. Neither shortcut is justified.

There is no executable entry price, target allocation or rank based on this record. Before consideration, reconcile G2/G3, obtain official liquidity and revise the cash model with dated bank/claim terms. Then require a funded base case meeting at least 15% net INR return and a survivable bear case at a position that suits actual whole-lot liquidity. No portfolio suitability facts about the user are assumed. No Git or website publication was performed.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved. Not rank-eligible; no current buy recommendation.** Safety Controls & Devices Limited is an electrical-infrastructure EPC contractor, not a safety-equipment manufacturer with a demonstrated recurring product franchise. Its apparent low earnings multiple is not sufficient compensation evidence when cash conversion, historical accounting and current funding cannot be reconciled reliably.

FY26 revenue increased to ₹117.01 crore and PAT to ₹14.42 crore. Yet CFO was **negative ₹11.22 crore**, trade receivables plus retention reached **₹158.71 crore**, and unrestricted cash was only **₹0.22 crore** at 31 March 2026. A ₹48 crore fresh IPO followed in April. This changes the funding picture materially, but audited March cash cannot be added to gross IPO money and called October unrestricted cash. Fees, restricted objects, debt repayment and subsequent working-capital use matter.

The strongest adverse evidence is the original FY25 ₹16.56 crore vendor-loss charge to reserves, subsequent restatement differences, a genuine February 2026 bank-guarantee/overutilisation default, and weak cash conversion. The strongest counterevidence is equally important: the lender confirmed regularisation on 13 April, Acuité upgraded to BB+/Stable/A4+ on 31 August after the curing period, and FY26 carries an unmodified audit opinion and satisfactory IFC opinion. **Historical default is not a claim of current default; accounting contradictions are not proof of fraud.** [E01–E10]

The common-entry monthly model gives no ordinary shareholder return for the base case because terminal debt retirement and operating reserves are not cash-funded. The bull case survives and produces a conditional ₹213.72 exit price and 21.03% net annual return, but requires better collections and margins than a conservative underwriting case. It is a hypothesis to falsify, not a price target.

Canonical factors are reused, never substituted between scores. BQS = .20 GOV + .20 MOAT + .12 REV + .10 DUR + .12 CAP + .10 CASH + .08 BAL + .08 EXEC. GQS = .40 REV + .20 DUR + .15 EARN + .15 CAP + .10 CASH. IAS = .25 Q + .35 R + .20 D + .10 P + .10 L, where Q is final BQS. Each vector sums exactly to 1 using Decimal arithmetic.

BQS known contribution is 3.82, missing weight .12: the unrenormalised bound is 3.94–5.02. GQS known contribution is 4.85, missing weight .15: raw bound 5.00–6.35. Persistent CASH≤3 caps a computable GQS at 5; it does **not** convert missing CAP into an invented GQS 5. IAS known contribution is .60, missing weight .80: bound 1.40–8.60. These are missing-data bounds, not statistical confidence intervals. Raw and final composites remain NS; no midpoint, zero substitution or renormalisation is used.

| Factor | Score | Confidence | Decisive basis | Counterevidence | Evidence |

| DUR | 5 | Medium | Dated ₹327.62 crore backlog supports visibility, but tender concentration, billing and collection delays limit durability. | July backlog increased and transmission/renewable infrastructure demand offers opportunities. | E11, E13 |

| EXEC | 4 | Medium | Sales/operating margins improved, but receivable forecast was missed and project cash/default chronology show execution strain. | Revenue grew 14.09% in FY26 and order book remains substantial. | E11, E13, E22 |
| EARN | 3 | Medium | GST correction, vendor-loss reserve treatment, tax credit and EPS denominator changes weaken repeatability of headline growth. | FY26 is unmodified and PAT remains positive without prior-tax credit. | E03, E04, E21, E24 |
| R | NS | Low | Reliable base-case funded ordinary return is not established, and entry price remains secondary. | A fully specified bull scenario survives and yields a conditional return, not the base return used for R. | E17, E23 |

REV uses the preselected comparable three-year window because five-year comparability fails. The ≥30% schedule starts at 9 and limited verified comparable history applies the ceiling 8; no extra small-base penalty is applied. CAP is not inferred from headline ROCE. CASH measures realised conversion, EARN accounting repeatability, BAL dated financing resilience, and D impairment severity. The adverse same facts are not repeatedly used for unexplained discretionary haircuts. A one-point GOV change shifts BQS known bounds .20; a one-point REV change shifts BQS .12 and GQS .40. Gates remain binding.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
Safety designs, procures, installs, tests and commissions electrical substations and allied works. Its disclosed technical envelope includes AIS substations up to 400 kV and GIS up to 220 kV, with solar, fire-fighting and hospital/infrastructure work. These are principally project businesses: qualification and award lead to equipment procurement, construction, certification, milestone billing and collection. They are not subscription revenues. Management reports 19 commissioned substations and 60 employees; outsourced suppliers and project execution resources are therefore important. [RHP pp 136–156; E11]

A sale is not cash. Percentage-of-completion/certification, customer advances, vendor advances and 15–30% retention terms produce long financing cycles. Materials consumed were ₹81.25 crore against FY26 revenue ₹117.01 crore. Procurement pass-through and changing contract mix can move sales and margins without equivalent proprietary value added. Public-sector/utility customers can lower ultimate counterparty-loss risk while increasing certification and payment timing risk. Principal disclosed geography is Uttar Pradesh and Bihar; government tender demand does not guarantee company-level order access or settlement.

No material acquisition, amalgamation, divestment or revaluation is identified over the disclosed ten-year lookback. The RHP says there are no subsidiaries/associates and at one point no joint venture, but separately describes a 19 January 2024 joint-bid deed with K. Ramachandra Rao Transmission & Projects Private Limited for BSPTCL NIT 38/PR/2023 with joint/several responsibilities. This could be a contractual consortium rather than an equity JV. We do not invent an acquired subsidiary or conclude the obligations are zero. Obtain the deed, work-share and guarantee schedule before closing scope risk. [RHP pp 174–175; E12]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
Tender credentials, technical capability, bank-guarantee access and completion history create real entry friction. They do not establish switching costs, pricing power, brand dominance or recurring service economics. In FY25 the largest customer represented 65.07% of revenue, the largest three 94.10%, and top five 97.80%; the largest supplier represented 56.64% of purchase/direct-expense concentration and top three 66.61%. The supplier table's misleading column label is not treated as a revenue ratio. Ten months to January 2026 top customer concentration eased to 41.55%, but top three remained 90.91%. [RHP; E11]

There is no verified market-share numerator/denominator, proprietary-IP economic record or price-volume realization bridge. MOAT 4 reflects a capable small contractor with qualifications, not a demonstrated protected franchise. Further growth may require both more procurement credit and more BG collateral, limiting the apparent asset-light advantage.

The economic peers below are independently read primary annual reports at the common FY25 period. Margins are ratios, not percentage points. They are not a current valuation peer group.

Viviana is the closest electrical T&D/substation EPC comparison; its negative CFO shows the industry's working-capital problem is not unique to Safety. Rajesh Power is much larger with EHV/HV cables/substations and proportionate joint-venture accounting, and also had negative CFO. Its current receivables exclude separately presented long retention, so a simplistic DSO comparison would be misleading. Oriana combines solar EPC with RESCO/SPV economics. Its ₹290.49 crore CFO includes ₹40.28 crore FD release, ₹141.52 crore payable growth and ₹317.56 crore other-liability growth; it is not pure cash generated from collected profit. Excluding FD release and reversing the operating-classified debt decrease gives ₹250.51 crore, still requiring funding-composition interpretation. No same-date primary peer-price/capital set was obtained, so current peer P/E rankings are NS. [E18–E20]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.content_markdown:
Reported net-GST revenue grew from ₹47.88 crore FY23 to ₹44.71 crore FY24, ₹102.56 crore FY25 and ₹117.01 crore FY26. The three-year CAGR is **34.70%**, using exactly three annual intervals. Annual additions are −₹3.16 crore, +₹57.85 crore and +₹14.45 crore. FY24 contracted 6.61%, FY25 increased 129.38%, and FY26 increased 14.09%. This is uneven project scaling, not a stable 35% annual engine. [E02,E21]

The revenue endpoints are same-entity and net-GST, and FY25 revenue reconciles between original and restated records. No acquired revenue is identified, making organic-like entity growth the defensible basis, with Medium confidence. An exact organic volume/real-price split is **not** available: equipment prices, pass-through procurement, contract mix and POC recognition could contribute. Thus the report does not call 34.70% underlying physical-volume growth.

Original FY21 sales were ₹32.25314 crore, not the rounded ₹27 crore sometimes displayed by aggregators, but the GST/presentation basis cannot be reconciled sufficiently to FY26. Five-year CAGR is NS rather than a selectively convenient number. Ten-year CAGR is also NS. FY23 original, later-comparative and prospectus profits/cash differ; these cannot be used interchangeably to claim a decade of quality growth. The listed history since April 2026 is too short to infer stable trading or minority-shareholder outcomes.

RHP current orders included TUSCO ₹83.53 crore dated 19 August 2025 and RVNL ₹55.65 crore dated 19 December 2025. The later Acuité aggregate unexecuted order book was ₹327.62 crore at 31 July 2026 versus ₹314.81 crore a year earlier. These dates/scopes differ, so the two orders are not added to the total and the old single-order DRHP table is not called current backlog. A complete opening backlog + intake − execution − cancellation bridge and project-level margin/collection schedule remain ND. [E13]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
The growth opportunity is real: transmission/substation additions and renewable grid integration require EPC capacity. But company-level reinvestment is dominated by working capital and collateral, not just PPE. FY26 cash capex was only ₹0.0351 crore; this does not explain negative CFO, nor establish that growth needs no capital. FY26 IC grew ₹36.42 crore, driven by ₹37.33 crore additional operating working capital while restricted-BG deposits released ₹0.56 crore. [financial_inputs.json reinvestment_bridges]

IC is reconciled from both sides with component-level records. Financing IC = equity + gross debt + net DTL + income-tax provision − unrestricted cash; required restricted BG collateral remains invested capital. Asset-side IC includes PPE, collateral, receivables, retention, inventory, vendor/government/security advances and prepaids, less non-interest operating liabilities. FY26 financing IC is ₹113.8132 crore versus asset-side ₹113.8133 crore, a ₹0.0001 crore rounding difference. FY25 original opening IC ₹77.3974 crore yields average IC ₹95.6053 crore. At an explicit 25.17% normalized tax assumption, FY26 EBIT ₹26.0469 crore gives NOPAT ₹19.4909 crore and indicative ROIC **20.39%**. This is not an audited project IRR. [E01,E03,E24]

Reinvestment bridges, in ₹ lakh: FY24 restated ΔIC 1565.57 = .53 capex −14.96 DA +1689.68 ΔONWC −106.09 BG −3.61 security +.02 rounding. FY25 restated ΔIC 2956.07 = 472.03 −31.60 +2256.03 +264.02 −4.40 −.01. FY26 original ΔIC 3641.61 = 3.51 −37.18 +3732.67 −56.17 −1.22. Financing and asset components are retained for every observation, not reconstructed from revenue multiples.

The one-year incremental proxy is ΔNOPAT/ΔIC using original FY25–26; it is diagnostic only because margin improvement, old-contract recognition and reserve losses distort causation. A valid three/five-year incremental-return numerator and denominator cannot be isolated across the accounting discontinuities. CAP remains NS. No high ROIC is used to give a second boost to REV or a compounder designation.

The forecast requires incremental fixed capital above an explicitly hypothetical ₹150 crore sales envelope, maintenance capex and full target operating working capital; added capacity faces a three-month qualification lag. These are A, not management disclosed capacity plans. Growth earns value only if incremental cash returns exceed the 16–22% model discount rate; faster sales financed by mounting receivables can destroy rather than create value.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
Promoters held 9,199,305 shares or 46.40% in the issuer's 10 April 2026 pattern. The official October capital master reconciles total issued shares, but the April 15,410,999 locked shares are not treated as October free float. No unverified pledge-free/current-beneficial-holding assertion is made. [E15,E16]

The major stewardship question is the FY25 ₹16.5565 crore vendor-advance loss charged directly to reserves. On the original FY25 result, charging that loss through profit would turn ₹7.6441 crore PAT into an approximately ₹8.9124 crore loss. The prospectus restatement instead assigns ₹2.2335 crore loss to FY23 and ₹2.8863 crore to FY24, with earlier losses in opening reserves. Those losses are not charged again to FY25 in this analysis. Counterparty identity, relatedness, board approval, recoverability attempts and allocation rationale require primary records. This is a documented treatment issue, not a finding of diversion or fraud. [E03]

FY26 MD remuneration was ₹34 lakh, Abhishek remuneration ₹16.2 lakh, and sitting fees ₹10.2 lakh. The MD loan bridge broadly reconciles: opening 69.81 + received 296.56 − repaid 100.69 = 265.68 lakh, close to note 6/board 265.67 but not note 27's 262.19. Note 6 classifies short-term, whereas the board narrative says non-current. Anjali remuneration 3.25 lakh in the board table versus nil in note 27 also needs reconciliation. These are specific small inconsistencies, not an invented large RPT siphoning. Proposed MD compensation from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2029 was fixed ₹80 lakh plus 2% of Section 198 profit and business reimbursements; AGM approval outcome is unverified, so proposed terms are not called approved. [E06]

Earlier RPT history is also qualified: the FY24 original note28 shows Rajnish remuneration ₹60 lakh, Anjali ₹1.2 lakh and Abhishek ₹16.2 lakh in each of FY23 and FY24. FY24 Rajnish loans taken ₹147.05 lakh and repaid ₹96.40 lakh suggest a ₹50.65 lakh movement, but the printed table places ₹50.65 lakh under FY23 receivable, with no FY24 closing payable. That anomalous layout is preserved, not silently repaired into a promoter-loan roll-forward. FY22 note25 RPT tables are effectively blank, which is not evidence that no transactions occurred. Full five-year RPT completeness is therefore not established. [O22 note25; O24 note28]

Audit trail by year: FY21 unmodified with COVID emphasis; CARO referenced but missing from the accessible original, IFC clean. FY22 unmodified/CARO read; referenced IFC and own cash-flow page missing. FY23 unmodified/CARO/IFC; edit-log rule not yet applicable until April 2023. FY24 qualified for GST-inclusive grossing, IFC described as inapplicable, edit-log wording only confirms a feature. The issuer FY25 file does not include the full original opinion/CARO/IFC; RHP disclosure and the original reserve note are not substitutes for claiming the missing original opinion was read. FY26 unmodified opinion and satisfactory IFC, but CARO records Canara payment delays ₹290,840 for 56 days and ₹286,359 for 28 days, no internal-audit system, and audit-trail feature existence rather than complete operation/tamper/preservation assurance. [E04,E05; original_audit_extract.json]

RHP discloses Doshi resignation 11 August 2025 and Panchal appointment 12 August; FY26 CARO says no auditor resignation. The resolution could concern scope/timing/interpretation, but no reconciliation is supplied. RHP and final prospectus no-default assertions conflict with the subsequently established February bank event. Note 32's ₹200 lakh FY25 Section 42 penalty becomes nil FY26, while RHP describes cheque, tax and ROC matters. Nil closing accounting balance or audit wording is not a settlement order. Obtain orders and current case status before claiming clearance. [E05–E10]

Execution is measured by collection as well as awards. The prospectus FY26 receivable projection ₹96.52 crore was below actual ₹121.60 crore excluding retention, a ₹25.08 crore miss. Forecast 240 days and agency 379 days use potentially different denominators; they are not subtracted as if identical. Low material cost helped FY26 margin expansion; sustained project economics, rather than a procurement-price benefit alone, must be demonstrated.

### Dated representations versus delivery

| RHP management working-capital estimate, 26 February 2026: FY26 trade receivables ₹96.5246 crore and projected holding 240 days | Audited 31 March trade receivables ₹121.6044 crore, with retention ₹37.1049 crore separately; agency debtor metric379 days | Like-for-like receivable balance missed by ₹25.0798 crore; day definitions differ. Negative execution evidence, not an invented cash shortfall of that exact amount. |

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.content_markdown:
At conditional ₹79.06 and 19,826,999 shares, market capitalisation is ₹156.75 crore. Current-share FY26 P/E is 10.87× and ex-prior-tax-credit 11.69×. The common shortcut 79.06/10.60 materially understates P/E after IPO dilution. March debt/cash plus October post IPO market cap produces only a stale-date EV bridge, not current EV. Neither EPS normalisation nor a low multiple resolves negative cash conversion or source discrepancies. R and P remain NS.

### Funding and timing model

All scenarios start with 31 March 2026 observed balances and the same seven-period analytical bridge to 19 October 2026. No H1FY27 cash flow was available within cutoff. April 1–12 daily cash movements are unobserved; IPO availability on 13 April is assumed from listing/cure chronology, not bank statement. Ordinary April flows settle on 30 April. This explicit gap means the model is not a verified historical survival reconstruction. Post entry bear/base/bull divergence begins 20 October and first modeled payment 19 November 2026.

Opening available cash ₹.2209 crore is separate from ₹14.4084 crore pledged FD and ₹.3481 crore government advance, neither spent. IPO gross ₹48 crore less detailed fees ₹5.76 crore yields ₹42.24 crore earmarked: ₹6 crore debt repayment, ₹31.5 crore eligible WC and ₹4.74 crore GCP. Actual gross issuance is not issued twice in shares. WC proceeds release only against supplier/operating cash payments, not again as a reduction of ΔWC. Unspent pools are excluded from terminal cash. The competing ₹43.14 crore net-proceeds summary is tested as ₹.90 crore fee relief, not silently used. Fees ex/inclusive GST wording is ambiguous; an additional ₹1.0368 crore 18%-of-detailed-fee sensitivity is also retained. Already incurred ₹.207 crore IPO expenses are within the fee budget, not added again. [E14]

Opening statutory dues ₹4.0466 crore settle 30 April A; income tax ₹6.087 crore in four ₹1.52175 crore installments June/September/December/March A; current gratuity ₹.10 crore September A. Prepayment fee ₹.24 crore is 4% of ₹6 crore A, separate from principal and IPO fees. Long gratuity ₹.2322 crore is retained terminal claim. Payroll/expense/customer-advance liabilities remain in ONWC and are not paid a second time. First year current maturities ₹5.0161 crore are modeled monthly in addition to IPO ₹6 crore repayment, with 0/50/100% overlap sensitivities because exact facility allocation is unverified. Full overlap preserves more terminal debt, not free cash. Remaining opening debt incurs 20% annual interest A, sensitised 16–24%, and is cash-retired once at terminal. April charges the full opening debt for 12 days before the assumed 13 April repayment and the post-repayment balance for 18 days; this adds ₹0.03945 crore versus incorrectly applying the lower debt throughout April. Actual penal interest and bank debit dates remain unverified.

Each month has two supplier front/collection cycles; 60% of cost is paid before each collection. Every event checks ₹.10 crore minimum cash, not just year-end. Receivables, inventory, retention/vendor assets, payables and accruals are explicit stock rollforwards. Growth fixed capex pays upfront above the ₹150 crore inflation-adjusted envelope at ₹.06 per incremental revenue ₹1; qualification lag 3 months. Maintenance is max(.5% sales, 5% opening PPE); depreciation 8% PPE; tax 25.17% on positive profit, with no invented tax-loss refund. These are assumptions, not audited contractual terms.

Existing ₹14.4084 crore BG collateral remains blocked. Additional cash-funded collateral rises with peak annual revenue above the audited ₹117.0147 crore base, at 15% / 10% / 8% in bear / base / bull. No release is assumed. It is a separate intraperiod payment, does not qualify for IPO working-capital releases in this model, enters operating capital, and is reinvested at terminal growth. Ratios 0% / 5% / 15% / 20% are separately tested. At terminal, additional collateral reinvestment equals growth × collateral ratio × the greater of final-year realised revenue and ending annual sales run-rate. This retains the full marginal requirement, rather than growing only collateral above the historical revenue offset. It replaces, rather than adds to, g × existing additional collateral within terminal ONWC growth. Actual bank collateral terms are ND; assuming no additional collateral silently would overstate growth affordability.

Whole-share equity at ₹60 incurs 6% fee and cannot exceed ₹1.038006 crore gross or 173,001 shares, the 20 million authorised headroom. No automatic increase in authorised capital or unlimited rescue is assumed. ₹40/60/79.06 issue price and zero-bank sensitivity are explicit. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear case is that apparently profitable EPC growth keeps consuming cash through uncertified receivables, retention and vendor advances; a supplier or BG event then forces repayment while tender customers delay cash. Historical vendor loss and February BG invocation show this mechanism is not purely abstract. A 35% revenue fall is below the FY25 largest customer 65.07% exposure, but is still an analyst stress, not a forecast customer loss. Receivable 10%/inventory 10% haircuts and ₹5 crore BG call are assumptions, not discovered impairments.

The no-finance stress breaches a supplier front payment; bounded bank/equity only delays breach. Capital can then be impaired through forced asset collection discounts, lien priority, project termination penalties, dilutive capital or insolvency costs. We do not report a normal IRR after such breach. The balance-sheet book equity is not a liquidation floor: BG FD is encumbered, receivables require certification, current liabilities and statutory claims have priority, and missing claim details prevent a robust net recoverable value. Downside can be severe, including complete equity loss; no fabricated probability is assigned.

The decisive thesis-break variable is **cash collection net of new working-capital commitments**, not revenue or announced orders. Countercase: public clients eventually settle, IPO working capital restores execution and Acuite upgrade persists. Evidence needed to choose between these cases is post-cutoff monitoring, not optimistic multiple expansion at the cutoff.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.content_markdown:
Required gross price CAGRs are 37.97% for 5× in 5 years, 58.49% for 10× in 5 years, 17.46% for 5× in 10 years and 25.89% for 10× in 10 years. Net return after costs is lower; dilution means enterprise growth must outpace per share growth. Tests use both base and bull cash economics, 10/20/30/40/50/60% sales growth, both horizons and both targets. They retain every trial's revenue, new operating capital, finance debt/equity/fees, shares, survival and 8× EBIT lower-multiple crosscheck.

| 5 | 5× | base | None | 0 / 6 |
| 5 | 5× | bull | None | 0 / 6 |
| 5 | 10× | base | None | 0 / 6 |
| 5 | 10× | bull | None | 0 / 6 |
| 10 | 5× | base | None | 0 / 6 |
| 10 | 5× | bull | 20.00% | 2 / 6 |
| 10 | 10× | base | None | 0 / 6 |
| 10 | 10× | bull | 30.00% | 1 / 6 |

None is called probable merely because a formula reaches the target. Very high growth requires additional qualified projects, BG access, procurement credit, staffing and collection capacity; a ₹327.62 crore July backlog does not establish decade-long replenishment. Some cash paths fail even when terminal business value looks large. Any mathematically successful bull trial is classified **Speculative / unsupported**, not a multibagger candidate, until comparable accounts, sustainable incremental returns and funded order access are demonstrated. Full results in multibagger_tests.json prevent terminal multiple-only storytelling.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved; not a compounder; not an investable or multibagger ranking entry.** BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS with explicit coverage and bounds. A governance Avoid label would require stronger substantiated adverse evidence, while a clean low P/E buy would require much better reliability, cash and execution evidence. Neither shortcut is justified.

There is no executable entry price, target allocation or rank based on this record. Before consideration, reconcile G2/G3, obtain official liquidity and revise the cash model with dated bank/claim terms. Then require a funded base case meeting at least 15% net INR return and a survivable bear case at a position that suits actual whole-lot liquidity. No portfolio suitability facts about the user are assumed. No Git or website publication was performed.
